label: Denver ↔ Yellowstone RV Trip, July 2026 (Fishing Bridge x2)

trip.title: Denver ↔ Yellowstone RV Trip
trip.notes: 1,400 included miles (overage charged per mile). Return RV full; drop by 10:30 am Wed 15 Jul (Drop & Go). Fly home afternoon.

days.title: Denver → Casper
days.summary: Pick up RV from Road Bear depot, big grocery shop at Walmart, then drive north on I-25 through Cheyenne and Douglas to Casper. Check in Casper KOA.

schedule.text: Land at DEN. Bags claim at 11:45, then Road Bear shuttle / Uber to the branch (~20 min).
Pickup appointment, 6586 Brighton Blvd. Walkthrough 60–90 min, paperwork, deposit.
Big shop — Walmart Supercenter, 5990 Dahlia St (5 min from the branch): a week of water, food, snacks, coffee, sealed/zip bags for bear-safe storage, sunscreen, bug spray, torches.
North on I-25. ~17:45 fuel & leg-stretch at Wheatland (~140 mi). Summer light to ~20:45.
Arrive Casper; cook in or grab dinner.

days.title: Casper → Fishing Bridge
days.summary: Stop at Lou Taubert Ranch Outfitters in Casper (opens 10 AM). Drive US-20/26 west through Wind River Canyon and stop at Thermopolis Hot Springs State Park. Continue through Cody before entering Yellowstone via the East Entrance to Fishing Bridge RV Park.

schedule.text: Lou Taubert Ranch Outfitters, 125 E 2nd St (opens 10:00) — six floors of Western wear; cowboy hats & boots for the family. ~1h30.
Depart Casper; Wind River Canyon en route (2,500-ft walls).
Thermopolis — lunch + a soak at Hot Springs State Park (free State Bath House, ~20-min soak). Wyoming Dinosaur Center next door for the kids.
Depart; quick fuel in Cody (~17:10), then the scenic Wapiti Valley and over Sylvan Pass (8,500 ft — steady).
Arrive Fishing Bridge. Full hookups, showers, laundry. Hard-sided rigs only — store all food inside. FILL FUEL IN CODY before the park.

days.title: Dawn Hayden Valley, then Geysers Loop
days.fromTo: Fishing Bridge → Hayden Valley → West Thumb → Old Faithful → Fishing Bridge
days.summary: Up at dawn for the best wildlife window in the park — Hayden Valley bison, elk, and maybe a grizzly. Then west via West Thumb Geyser Basin, Old Faithful & the Upper Geyser Basin, and Grand Prismatic Spring, looping back to Fishing Bridge RV Park for a second night (Madison Campground was fully booked).

schedule.text: Dawn wildlife drive — Hayden Valley (25 min north): first light is the best wildlife window in the park — big bison herds, elk, and a good chance of grizzly or wolf at distance. Bring binoculars; stay 100 yds from bears/wolves.
Back for breakfast at the campsite.
West Thumb Geyser Basin — colourful hot springs right on the lakeshore; a quick warm-up boardwalk.
Old Faithful & Upper Geyser Basin — check the predicted eruption time, walk the boardwalks (Castle, Grand, Morning Glory Pool) and step inside the historic Old Faithful Inn. Lunch here.
Midway Geyser Basin — Grand Prismatic Spring, the largest hot spring in the US. Overlook trail open; check the NPS app for closures. Optional: a dip on Firehole Canyon Drive on the way.
Depart Midway, retracing through Old Faithful and West Thumb back to Fishing Bridge.
Back at Fishing Bridge — same site for a second night. Full hookups, showers, laundry.

days.title: Fishing Bridge → Canyon → Cody & the Rodeo
days.fromTo: Fishing Bridge → Canyon Village → Cody, WY
days.summary: Morning at the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone — Artist Point and the Lower Falls, via Hayden Valley both ways. Exit via the East Entrance down the Wapiti Valley. Afternoon at the Buffalo Bill Center of the West, then the Cody Nite Rodeo at 8 PM (free KOA shuttle at 7 PM).

schedule.text: Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone — Artist Point and the Lower Falls.
Depart Fishing Bridge → Canyon via Hayden Valley (another good wildlife window) — 45 min. Artist Point, Lower Falls overlooks.
Depart Canyon → Fishing Bridge via Hayden Valley — wildlife roll south (bison, elk, often grizzly or wolf at distance; stay 100 yds back).
Depart Fishing Bridge → East Entrance → Cody via the gorgeous Wapiti Valley.
Arrive Cody — Buffalo Bill Center of the West (firearms, Plains Indian, art, natural history, Buffalo Bill wings; 2–3h, closes 6 PM). Wear the new hats! Check in at the KOA and have a swim.
KOA free rodeo shuttle leaves camp at 7:00 PM sharp — no driving or parking the rig.
Cody Nite Rodeo — ~2 hours of bronc & bull riding, barrel racing and a kids' calf scramble. The shuttle brings you back.

days.title: Cody → Casper
days.summary: Relaxed half-day drive south through the Wind River Canyon. Optional second soak at Thermopolis Hot Springs en route. Arrive Casper mid-afternoon for the KOA pool and an easy evening before the final push home.

schedule.text: Easy morning in Cody — finish the Buffalo Bill Center, or browse Sheridan Ave for more Western bits.
Depart Cody.
Thermopolis — a second soak at Hot Springs State Park and lunch, if you fancy it.
Depart Thermopolis.
Arrive Casper — mid-afternoon with time for the KOA pool and an easy evening before the last stretch south.

days.title: Casper → Fort Collins (early finish!)
days.summary: Unhurried drive south on I-25 into Colorado. Arrive Fort Collins / Lakeside KOA by early afternoon — enjoy paddle boats, fishing, mini-golf and the pool. Evening: Old Town Fort Collins and the breweries for a relaxed last dinner.

schedule.text: Unhurried start; drive south on I-25 into Colorado.
Fort Collins / Lakeside KOA — check in early and make the most of it: paddle boats and fishing on the lake, mini-golf, the pool and the jumping pillow.
Old Town Fort Collins (the model for Disney's Main Street USA) and the breweries for a relaxed last dinner.

days.title: Fort Collins → Denver Airport
days.fromTo: Fort Collins, CO → Denver International Airport
days.summary: Easy morning drive south on I-25. Drop RV at Road Bear depot by 10:30 AM (Drop & Go — no tank-dump or clean needed). Transfer to DEN; fly home.

schedule.text: Depart; top the tank to FULL near the branch (return full — stations on Brighton Blvd / near I-270).
Arrive 6586 Brighton Blvd. Drop-off window 8:00–10:30 AM. Drop & Go (Platinum Plus) — no tank-dumping or final clean, just hand it back (~30–45 min).
Transfer to DEN (~30 min). Allow plenty of time at the airport.

places.name: Casper KOA Journey
places.notes: Nights 1 & 5. Full hookups, pool, dog park. Just off I-25.

places.name: Fishing Bridge RV Park
places.notes: Nights 2 & 3 (2 nights — Madison Campground was fully booked, so we kept the same site instead of moving). Full hookups (hard-sided RVs only — bear country). Reservation required.

places.name: Cody / Yellowstone East KOA
places.notes: Night 4. Free nightly rodeo shuttle (departs KOA 7:00 PM sharp). Two pools, hot tub, free pancakes. Book direct — online booking sometimes off, call to confirm.

places.name: Fort Collins / Lakeside KOA
places.address: 1910 Lakeside Resort Ln, Fort Collins, CO 80524
places.notes: Night 6. Full hookups. Paddle boats, fishing lake, mini-golf, pool, jumping pillow. Easy I-25 access for final morning.

places.name: Road Bear RV Depot
places.notes: Pickup Day 1 (1:00–4:00 PM appointment). Return by 10:30 AM Day 7 (Drop & Go — no tank dump or clean needed).

places.name: Walmart Supercenter (big shop)
places.notes: Major grocery and supply run before hitting the road. Stock up for 7 days: water, food, coffee, sealed bags for bear storage, sunscreen, bug spray, torches.

places.name: Lou Taubert Ranch Outfitters
places.notes: Opens 10 AM. Six floors of Western wear — cowboy hats & boots for the family. ~1h30.

places.name: Hot Springs State Park
places.notes: World's largest mineral hot spring. Free State Bath House (~20-min soak). Wyoming Dinosaur Center next door for the kids. Great leg-stretch on Days 2 & 5.

places.name: Buffalo Bill Center of the West
places.notes: World-class Western museum (5 museums in one). Allow 2–3 hours. Open daily, closes 6 PM. Wear the cowboy hats!

places.name: Cody Nite Rodeo (Stampede Park)
places.notes: Gates open 7 PM, rodeo starts 8 PM every night June–Aug. Free shuttle from Cody KOA departs 7:00 PM sharp. ~$25–79/seat.

places.name: Hayden Valley
places.notes: Best wildlife viewing in the park. Dawn on Day 3 is prime time — bison herds, elk, grizzly or wolf at distance. Also rolled through on Day 4 en route to Fishing Bridge. Drive slowly; stay 100 yds from bears/wolves.

places.name: Mud Volcano
places.notes: Bubbling mud pots and fumaroles on the road between Fishing Bridge and Hayden Valley. Short boardwalk loop. The sulphurous smell is part of the experience!

places.name: Artist Point
places.notes: Classic overlook of the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone and Lower Falls. Short walk from parking. Don't miss it.

places.name: Canyon Village
places.notes: Visitor center, gift shop, gas. Start of the North and South Rim drives to the Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone.

places.name: West Thumb Geyser Basin
places.notes: Unique geothermal features right on the shore of Yellowstone Lake. Boardwalk loop ~1 mile. Warm-up stop on Day 3 en route to Old Faithful.

places.name: Old Faithful
places.notes: Erupts every 60–110 min (avg ~90 min). Check predicted eruption times at the visitor center. Walk the Upper Geyser Basin (Castle, Grand, Morning Glory Pool). Lunch at Old Faithful Inn.

places.name: Grand Prismatic Spring
places.notes: Largest hot spring in the US. Rainbow colors best seen from the overlook trail (1 mile RT). Go early — boardwalk gets crowded by 9 AM. Check NPS app for trail closures.

places.name: Norris Geyser Basin
places.notes: Hottest and most dynamic geyser basin in the park. Not on the Day 4 route anymore (now via Hayden Valley instead of Norris) — optional detour if you have spare time. Two loop trails (Porcelain Basin ½ mi, Back Basin 1.5 mi).

places.name: Denver International Airport (DEN)
places.notes: Allow 1.5h minimum after returning the RV (10:30 drop) before heading airside.

places.name: Gibbon Falls
places.notes: 84-ft falls visible from the road between Madison and Norris. Not on the Day 4 route anymore (now via Hayden Valley) — optional detour only.

places.name: Firehole Canyon Drive (summer swim)
places.notes: One-way scenic drive with a legal swimming hole in the warm Firehole River. Open summer only. Near Madison/Old Faithful on Day 3 route — a fun optional extra.

places.name: Horsetooth Reservoir
places.notes: Great reservoir west of Fort Collins with hiking, kayaking, and swimming. Worth a morning stop on Day 7 if time allows.

places.name: New Belgium Brewing
places.notes: Colorado's largest craft brewery. Tours available; excellent taproom. Day 6 evening wind-down in Old Town Fort Collins.

places.name: Wyoming State Capitol
places.notes: Stunning Romanesque Revival capitol on I-25 corridor. 10-min stop if passing through Cheyenne on Days 1 or 6.

places.name: Cheyenne Frontier Days Old West Museum
places.notes: Celebrates the world's largest outdoor rodeo. Great carriage collection. Quick stop on I-25 route.

places.name: Buc-ee's Johnstown
places.notes: Giant travel plaza on I-25 exit 252. 100+ fuel pumps — perfect for filling the RV tank. Massive store: brisket sandwiches, kolaches, beaver nuggets, fudge, jerky. Stock up for the week heading into Yellowstone (Day 1), or grab road-trip treats on the way home (Day 7).

places.name: Terry Bison Ranch
places.address: 51 I-25 Service Rd E, Cheyenne, WY
places.notes: Bison ranch right on I-25 south of Cheyenne. Train ride to see bison up close. Good stop heading south on Day 6.

places.name: Glendo State Park
places.notes: Reservoir on the North Platte River. Good leg-stretch stop on Day 1 or Day 6 along I-25.

places.name: Ayers Natural Bridge
places.notes: Free county park; 30-ft natural stone arch over LaPrele Creek. 12-mile detour off I-25. Picnic area.

places.name: National Historic Trails Interpretive Center
places.notes: Excellent BLM-run museum covering Oregon, California, Mormon, and Pony Express trails through Casper. Worth 1–2 hours.

places.name: Fort Caspar Museum
places.notes: Reconstructed 1865 military fort with living-history exhibits. Near the Platte River Bridge.

places.name: Wind River Canyon Scenic Byway
places.notes: US-20 carves through this spectacular canyon — sheer 2,500-ft walls. You drive through it on Days 2 & 5. No detour needed.

places.name: Boysen State Park
places.notes: Reservoir at the mouth of Wind River Canyon. Fishing, boating. Quick stop on US-20 route on Days 2 or 5.

places.name: Wyoming Dinosaur Center
places.notes: One of the top dino museums in the US, with actual dig site tours. In Thermopolis — easy add-on to the hot springs stop.

places.name: Legend Rock Petroglyph Site
places.notes: Over 300 petroglyphs spanning thousands of years. Off paved road; check road conditions.

places.name: Buffalo Bill Dam & Visitor Center
places.notes: Historic arch dam in a spectacular gorge 6 miles west of Cody. Free to visit. Great photo stop entering or leaving Yellowstone.

places.name: Old Trail Town
places.notes: Collection of original 1800s frontier buildings relocated to one site. Cemetery of mountain men and outlaws. Admission ~$8.

places.name: Heart Mountain WWII Interpretive Center
places.notes: Moving museum on the Japanese American internment camp here 1942–45. Between Cody and the park. Allow 1–2 hours.

places.name: Lamar Valley
places.notes: The 'American Serengeti' — best wildlife viewing in the lower 48. Bison, wolves, bears, pronghorn. Dawn and dusk are prime time.

places.name: Mammoth Hot Springs
places.notes: Terraced travertine terraces — completely unique geology. Near the north entrance and Albright Visitor Center.

places.name: Tower Fall
places.notes: 132-ft waterfall. Short trail to overlook. Near Tower-Roosevelt junction on the northeast road.

places.name: Lake Yellowstone Hotel
places.notes: Historic 1891 hotel on Yellowstone Lake. Gorgeous views; even non-guests can walk the lobby and lakefront. Near Fishing Bridge.
